## The fix (two structural gaps, 2026-08-04 incident: T355/T356 had NO exit heartbeat — the runner was SIGKILLed in a load-16 %CPU sweep — and rows sat in_progress for hours)

1. PARENT-side exit records (tools/runner): the runner writes untracked/runs/<task>.json at LAUNCH (pid, pgid, launcher_pid, start, command) and REWRITES it at every exit path with the child's fate (exit code OR signal, end, wall, cpu, rss_mb, killed). A `kill -9` of the child leaves a COMPLETED record (signal=9 — the parent wrote it); a `kill -9` of the runner itself leaves the launch record with no exit fields — 'killed mid-flight', readable by the next reap/resume. Atomic write (tmp + rename); identity sanitized for the filename, matched on the record's stored task field.
2. `managent reap` [--close] (src/managent/main.zig): for each in_progress row — run-record pid alive => BACKED (never reaped; stalled is the progress watchdog's job); fresh heartbeat with no record => BACKED; dead runner with completed record => ORPHAN (run ended, row never closed); dead runner with launch-only record => ORPHAN (killed mid-flight); nothing at all => ORPHAN (no evidence). --close closes each orphan as `abandoned` with note 'reaped: <evidence>' under the store flock with a FRESH re-classification (a row that became backed between report and close is not closed). Never a verdict guess — an orphaned row is abandoned, not pass.
3. `resume` fleet-stall surface: in_progress rows with no live backing appear in a 'fleet stalls' section; '-- none --' when clean. Same classification as reap, read-only; degrades to '-- none --' on a fresh clone.
4. Guard-the-sweep doc (docs/infra/runner.md): a %CPU threshold kills workers indiscriminately (the 2026-08-04 cause); a crisis kill should target the offending row's process group via the run record's pgid.
